verdict.rationale: Better Auth documents a first-party SSO plugin supporting OIDC, OAuth2 and SAML 2.0, plus an organization plugin for multi-tenancy, so the core SSO capability exists. The evidence never shows SSO connections scoped to individual organizations, domain verification, or just-in-time user provisioning. A community note that some SSO/SAML features are enterprise-only adds uncertainty. Missing for 10: documented per-organization SSO connection binding, verified-domain routing/ownership checks, just-in-time provisioning of users into orgs, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can give each customer organization its own SSO connection with verified domains and just-in-time provisioning

citations.quote: This plugin supports OpenID Connect (OIDC), OAuth2 providers, and SAML 2.0.
SSO, SAML 2.0, SCIM, and directory sync.
Multi-tenancy built in. Teams, roles, invitations, and access control.
